name: sup-run-fallback-missing
notes: `vdelta run`'s 2-stage default baseline resolution (issue #72): when stage 2 (`previous-superset`) also abstains `baseline-missing`, the report returned to the consumer is stage 1's (`previous-comparable`) unchanged, not stage 2's. `C`'s only series-mate is `N` (selector `['src']`), a narrower run: `selectorRelation(N.selector, C.selector)` decides `'subset'`, so `N` is never a `previous-superset` candidate and stage 2 abstains `baseline-missing`/`determined` too (same shape as `sup-abstain-baseline-missing`). Because both stages land on `baseline-missing`, stage 1's report is what's returned -- this fixture intentionally does not assert on `comparability_detail.near_miss`, since stage 1's §5.4 near_miss disclosure may or may not be present depending on the vitest adapter's own comparison and is orthogonal to the fallback logic under test here.
